record.paper_title: A realist view of the electron: recent advances and unsolved problems
record.context_brief: Numerical intrinsic properties and electron size
record.original_question: In a realist extended-electron framework in which an electron is determined by intrinsic properties and is assumed to have a finite but unspecified volume V, can the exact numerical values of the electron's intrinsic properties and its actual size or volume be determined rather than left undefined?

evidence.quote:
The thesis elaborated in this paper uses a diﬀerent
method, which can be described by four assertions: (i)
An electron is determined by its intrinsic properties. (ii)
The exact numerical value of these properties, and con-
sequently the actual size of the electron remains unde-
ﬁned.

We start with a non-relativistic frame of reference, as-
suming that the electron has a ﬁnite volume V , which
is not speciﬁed, and that it moves with constant veloc-
ity ⃗ u= u⃗ eu.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider a realist model of the electron in which the electron is treated as a spatially extended object characterized solely by a collection of intrinsic properties (such as charge, mass, magnetic moment, spin angular momentum, and a characteristic volume V > 0). Assume a non-relativistic inertial frame in which the electron moves with constant velocity u along a fixed direction, and that the electron occupies a finite but a priori unspecified volume V. Within such a framework, determine whether it is possible to derive the exact numerical values of the electron's intrinsic properties together with its actual spatial size (volume V), rather than leaving these quantities undefined parameters of the model. Equivalently: produce a consistent extended-electron model that uniquely fixes the numerical values of all intrinsic properties and the volume of the electron, or prove that within the stated realist assumptions no such determination is possible.
artifact.status_search_result: No widely accepted determination of the electron's intrinsic size or a complete set of numerical intrinsic parameters from first principles is known. Experimental upper bounds on the electron radius continue to tighten (e.g., from Penning-trap and high-energy scattering experiments), but no theoretical framework has uniquely fixed these values; the question remains open in the realist/extended-electron literature.

status_evidence.title: Electron - Wikipedia (classical electron radius and size limits)
status_evidence.snippet: Experiments place upper limits on the electron's radius; the electron is treated as point-like in the Standard Model, and no theory derives its intrinsic numerical parameters from first principles.
status_evidence.claim: The size and intrinsic numerical parameters of the electron are not derived theoretically; only experimental bounds exist.
